title: Design System: Landlord Ledger — Bank Passbook

ink-soft.derivation: ink at 72% alpha — secondary text, labels, quiet rows

ink-faint.derivation: ink at 66% alpha — placeholders, the resting delete icons, the trend's sublabel, the least-important affordances

print-wash.derivation: print at 6% alpha — the balance rail's ground, rail hover, skeleton tint

print-soft.derivation: premixed print tint — the selected rail entry's ground; also the shadcn secondary/muted/accent slot (130 22% 93%)

rule.derivation: print at 38% alpha — the 1px hairline on rows, fields, dividers

page-title.purpose: Each route's own heading — the page's one h1; the product name in the header is a styled link home, not a heading. Body-scale bold ink; the world has no display face.

caption.purpose: The world's micro-label: field labels, table headers, strip labels, tfoot legend. Uppercase; tracking stops at 0.14em (fields), 0.16em (table headers), 0.18em (totals legends and stamp marks).

body.purpose: Form input text, tab labels, quiet controls; weight 600 on controls that act.

ledger.purpose: Every ledger cell — dates, descriptions, categories, amounts, balances. IBM Plex Mono with tabular numerals; categories and properties at 12.5px, the rest at the 13px ledger step.

totals-figure.purpose: The totals strip's Income / Expenses / Net — the largest figures on any page, still mono and tabular.

stamp-mark.purpose: Validation alert, the rotated delete-confirm question, and the export's acknowledgment stamp; the same 11px mono carries the sort arrows, the trend sublabel, and the Properties page's status marks and created-date line — the ramp's caption floor.

shadows.name: floating-md
shadows.purpose: The single soft shadow a floating surface is allowed — the Radix Select option list (Tailwind shadow-md).

shadows.name: floating-lg
shadows.purpose: The dialog panel (over its 35% ink wash), the destructive confirm (inline cluster at sm and up, fixed bottom sheet below), the export stamp, and the delete-undo snackbar — every floating surface casts this one soft shadow. The page at rest casts nothing.

motion.name: ease-print
motion.purpose: Exponential ease-out — the only authored easing.

motion.name: ledger-line-printed
motion.value: line-printed 500ms cubic-bezier(0.16, 1, 0.3, 1) both, fade-in 500ms cubic-bezier(0.16, 1, 0.3, 1) both
motion.purpose: The one authored motion: a row appearing after first paint wipes in left-to-right (clip-path inset(0 100% 0 0) to inset(0 0 0 0)) with a simultaneous fade — the balance figure lands last. First paint is still; a restored line (the undo's own small ceremony) prints back in too. Removed entirely under prefers-reduced-motion: reduce.

motion.name: state-transition
motion.purpose: Hover and focus are color/opacity states, not motion. The skeleton pulse is a stock utility; the one remaining spin (the deferred Add-Property modal) is stock too, not authored.

breakpoints.name: lg
breakpoints.purpose: The world's one behavior breakpoint: the rail expands or collapses (captions below, tooltips and toggle above), the header composes into one line, gutters widen to 2.25rem. useIsDesktop mirrors it via matchMedia, SSR-safe.

breakpoints.name: sm
breakpoints.purpose: The critique pass's mobile-discipline breakpoint (useMediaQuery, SSR-safe): the filters fold behind their 'Filters · N' disclosure, the ledger sheet holds print width (64rem) with a frozen date column, and the destructive confirm pins as a bottom sheet with 44px targets.

breakpoints.name: md
breakpoints.purpose: The Properties page's card grid steps 2-up here and 3-up at lg; no other behavior hangs on it.

passbookRules.name: hairline
passbookRules.detail: border-bottom: 1px solid rgba(46, 94, 78, 0.38) — every row, field edge, and internal divider.

passbookRules.name: totals
passbookRules.detail: The accountant's closing line, owned by exactly one side of its seam: .rule-totals on a top edge (the empty page's 'No entries' line), .rule-totals-b on the bottom edge of the row that closes the sheet — the last entry when no blank lines follow, the last blank line when they do. Spelled once each, deterministic against Tailwind's all-sides border-color utilities.

passbookRules.name: strip-edges
passbookRules.detail: The totals strip anchors itself with per-side utilities — border-t-print above, border-b-rule below — so no all-sides border-color can quietly win the anchor.

passbookRules.name: row-density
passbookRules.detail: --passbook-row, declared; realized as 0.625rem cell padding plus the 0.8125rem ledger line (~38-39px effective, one line — the destructive control lives in the reserved trailing cell, not in the prose).

passbookRules.name: control-density
passbookRules.detail: --passbook-control: every field, select trigger, and primary button is h-9.

passbookRules.name: blank-line
passbookRules.detail: The unfilled printed lines below the last entry — aria-hidden, pointer-events none, capped at fifteen.

passbookRules.name: radius
passbookRules.detail: The world's only corner (rounded-[2px]); the shadcn --radius base is re-pointed to 0.125rem so its lg/md steps collapse to the same 2px.

records.title: The stamp-red renegotiation
records.body: The original direction contract carried an over-budget mark in stamp red; it had no trigger — no budget concept exists in the product. No budget scope was added. Stamp-red's standing role is state marks only (destructive confirms, validation failures), never decoration. The over-budget row tint retired with the first-viewport plan; the built ledger's rows carry no such mark.

records.title: The deferred unknown-category edge
records.body: A transaction already in storage whose category string is not one of the app's category records is unreachable through the app's own form (the form's Category select offers only INCOME_CATEGORIES / EXPENSE_CATEGORIES) and can never be isolated by the ledger's category filter, which lists the same records. In the built code the row itself still renders, printing its raw stored category string in the Category cell and totaling into every summary; what is truly unreachable is its creation and its isolation, not its display. The edge is deferred rather than resolved — no semantics (validation, migration, display treatment) were decided, and this record exists so a future change decides them deliberately instead of inheriting an accident.

records.title: The two known contextual detector flags
records.body: Two real deviations survive every pass, both in the browser's chrome rather than the world's surfaces, and both are deliberately left alone: the scrollbar thumb's 5px radius (styles.css — the one corner outside the 2px system) and the devtools widget's own panel headings (the TanStack devtools mounted in the root route render h3s that trip the heading-order detector — dev chrome outside the world's landmarks, verified live in the critique pass). Neither is a pattern to extend; this record exists so a future audit recognizes them instead of re-litigating them.

narrative.overview:
The ledger reads the way a bank records money. The surface is a passbook page: ivory paper carries dense printed columns ruled in machine-print green hairlines, every date and peso figure is set in IBM Plex Mono with tabular numerals at print density, and a running balance marches down the right edge on a pale print wash so the eye can audit the month by running down the rail. The category's default — a dashboard of white cards floating on a gray ground — is refused wholesale: no cards, no shadows at rest, no chart rings. Every total is a ruled printed strip, the trend is a ruled table, and the empty ledger is a ruled line, never an illustrated panel.

Depth comes from rules and ground, never elevation. Ink navy does the reading; print green is the machine's voice — it owns the hairline grid, income figures, focus, selection, and the selected rail's wash; stamp red is held out for state marks only, the red of a rubber stamp landing on a confirmation or a rejected line. The browser surfaces carry the world too: selection, caret, native accents, link underlines, and scrollbars are all passbook-toned, the cheap tell that it was built rather than assembled. One authored motion exists — a newly recorded line prints itself onto the page — and nothing else animates; hover and focus are color states, not motion.

The world is an Operate surface: a landlord completing bookkeeping, where scanability, density, and trust outrank expression. The finished world covers the shell (rail, header, tabs, footer), the Overview, Transactions, and Properties views, and the shared primitives; the Properties page has had its passbook pass — ink contrast, squared bordered status marks, a ruled print-wash skeleton, hairline hover rules — and no longer ships default-template chrome. The record tells the truth about itself: the shell's footer names where the data lives on every page, an export lands a stamp acknowledgment, and a delete carries a five-second undo. Two deferrals remain, both recorded, not canonized: the Add-Property modal's native checkbox and pending spinner, and the unlinked Reports placeholder.
keyCharacteristics: Ivory paper ground (#fbf8f1), ink-navy type (#1b2a41), machine-print green hairline rules (#2e5e4e), stamp red (#a31621) reserved for state marks.
IBM Plex Mono with tabular numerals for every date and money figure, at print density (0.8125rem rows, ~2.375rem row rhythm).
Structure from rules — 1px hairlines everywhere, a 3px double totals rule for closing lines — never from shadows.
The running balance rail on a print wash down the ledger's right edge: the sheet opens chronological, and newest-first freezes the rail to the book's printed accumulation beneath a printed caveat.
One authored motion (the print-in), removed entirely under prefers-reduced-motion; a restored line prints back in too.
Honesty signals throughout: the footer's storage note, the export's stamp acknowledgment, the five-second delete undo that restores the original id.
2px corners everywhere: squared, printed form fields.

rules.name: The Stamp Rule
rules.body: Stamp red is a state mark only: destructive confirms and validation failures, always uppercase mono, always bordered or grounded — never a tint, tint never a decoration. If the red doesn't say "act on me" or "this was rejected," it doesn't appear.

rules.name: The Owned Browser Chrome Rule
rules.body: Selection prints as print green at 22% over paper with ink text; carets and native checkbox/radio accents are print green; links carry ink text over a 1px print underline at 3px offset, turning print green on hover; scrollbars are thin ink (34% alpha) on a transparent track with a paper-framed thumb. The world does not stop at the components.

rules.name: The Tabular Numerals Rule
rules.body: Every figure — money, dates, counts — is set in IBM Plex Mono with tabular numerals, so columns of pesos align down the page like a printed ledger. Money is formatted by the one formatMoney (₱, exactly two fraction digits everywhere) and dates by the one formatDate (en-US); no surface re-creates a local copy, and the sans face never sets a figure — the form's date and amount inputs print in the mono face, a date inside a field no less than a date on the page.

rules.name: The Flat Page Rule
rules.body: The page never casts shadows; a floating surface may cast one, softly. Hover on a page element changes color, never elevation.

rules.name: The One Authored Motion
rules.body: A row that appears after first paint prints itself onto the page: a left-to-right clip-path wipe plus a fade, 500ms, exponential ease-out, the balance figure landing last. First paint is still; a restored line (the undo's own small ceremony) prints back in too. prefers-reduced-motion removes it entirely. Nothing else is authored: hovers transition color/opacity only, the skeleton keeps its stock pulse, and the one remaining spin (the deferred Add-Property modal) is stock, not authored.

dos: Do set every figure in IBM Plex Mono with tabular numerals, formatted through the one formatMoney (₱, two fraction digits always) and the one formatDate.
Do build structure from the rules: 1px hairlines for rows, fields, and dividers; the 3px double totals rule for closing lines; print underlines for headers and the active tab.

Do keep the rail truthful: the sheet opens chronological (sorting removal is off), and newest-first freezes the rail to the book's printed accumulation beneath its printed caveat — the rail audits the book, not the sort.
Do name every totals claim honestly: the strip's label and aria-label total exactly the slice its page displays, and say which page semantics they carry ("Displayed ledger" vs "All entries").
Do say where the record lives and what each write did: the footer's storage note on every page, the export's stamp acknowledgment, and the delete's five-second undo restoring the original id.
Do keep every actionable surface on the 2px print outline (or the field ring) on focus-visible — rail, toggle, tabs, disclosure, delete control — never the browser default.
Do keep stamp red for state marks only — destructive confirms and validation failures — squared, uppercase mono, bordered or grounded.
Do keep one primary control per screen; everything else is quiet ink.
Do keep every overflow inside its own ruled region (tables and the tab row scroll; the main column floors at min-w-0) so the paper never leaks at 390px.
